After Kh3, Black again has Rh7#. So Rg8+ forces the king to move, and then Black delivers Rh7# on every option. This is a back rank mate pattern!

**Best move:** Rg8+

**Main line:** Rg8+ Kh5 (or Kh4/Kh3) Rh7#

**Motif:** backRankMate

**Explanation:**
Black's loose b7 pawn distracted from a more critical threat. After Rg8+, the White king is forced away from the back rank—it has no escape squares. Black then delivers Rh7# on every king move. The king gets mated on the back rank because it cannot reach g7 or g8. Next time, when your opponent's king looks boxed in by the board edge or its own pawns, look for forcing checks that eliminate escape squares.
